dataset.name: Minnesota SPRUCE S1 Bog Peat Depth Determined by Push Probe and Ground Penetrating Radar: 2009-2010
description: This data set reports the thickness of peat for the S1 Bog, located in the Minnesota SPRUCE Experiment Site, measured directly with manual push probes on September 21 and 22, 2009, and measured by ground penetrating radar (GPR) across transects from January 26 to February 2, 2010 and June 2 to June 9, 2010. Also included are interpolated values of peat depth from both probe and GPR data for the S1 Bog at 1 meter square horizontal resolution.

The key objectives of these geophysical field surveys were to define the S1 peat depth, basin geometry, and to provide additional subsurface information for selecting the optimal locations for experimental plots (i.e., rows of chambers). GPR was specifically used to obtain better estimates of peat depths to refine the existing 3-D model of the S1 basin geometry and to provide high-density data on peat stratigraphy and examine variations in mineral soil near the proposed experimental plots.

measurementTechnique:
Direct Probe Measurements
During the September 2009 field campaign multiple push probe measurements were made using 0.5 cm diameter metal rods at 165 predetermined plot locations. Plots were laid out on a surveyed 20-m grid over the S1 Bog.

Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR)
During the winter 2010 campaign investigators used a Mala ProEx control unit and 50 MHz rough terrain antenna to obtain the GPR dataset. This antenna is ideally suited for such work as it can be easily carried in difficult terrain, such as that encountered in S1 bog due to the combination of vegetation density and significant, non-uniform snow accumulation (> 0.6 meter in places). The entire bog area was traversed and three common-midpoint (CMP) GRP surveys were performed at select locations.
For the summer 2010 campaign investigators used the same Mala ProEx control unit but utilized a 200 MHz antenna. The higher frequency antenna was selected based on the results of the winter survey and to provide higher resolution subsurface images. The summer measurements focused on four lines, oriented in a roughly E-W position (Figure 3), along the proposed boardwalk locations. For each surveyed line we performed two CMP profiles, ~ 10m apart, adjacent to the boardwalk location. This survey resulted in a total of 8 radargrams with detailed subsurface information.

Data Processing
Data processing is described in the provided users guide: SPRUCE S1 Bog Peat Depth Determined by Push Probe and GPR: 2009-2010.pdf
